entries.subtitle: i go with the flow
body: There have always been certain words I've been drawn to, merely for their existence:
" fatalistic, menace, bloom, homage, oblique, doodle, coincidence, liminal, silhouette, synthetic, shenanigans, artefact, parse, cherry….absurd".
Then one night, you wonder what is wrong with you, and find out there's a specific name for people like you. Logophile. WTF. Honestly, rude, given the fact that I like you, but only as a friend.

Talking about breaking off, drift apart, slip away, go your own way….you can call it….another lonely day. As I spend my last (lovely) day in my first full-time position at the rock research institution aka GFZ (not Dwayne Johnson).

Amusingly, I realized that once upon a time I came up the hill and it was raining, and then I left down the hill and it was raining, and I swear to god in the meantime we did not have any dubious deviation in weather.

entries.subtitle: one ticket, please
body: "Go to the left, find the stairs, go down, follow the red lines on the floor," three instructions to follow is still manageable, I thought to myself as I tricked the ticket seller into giving me a student discount.
A modern, ugly concrete bench, white point-focused artificial LED light, uncomfortable air conditioner settings and suspiciously familiar shoes.

Subject A attempted to induce a prolonged visual fixation on me. I knew wearing my maybelline red lipstick was a tactically dangerous thing to do, though I never considered its impact on inanimate objects.
Oh boy, you better keep an eye out at the Gemäldegalerie as the eerie saints of the past might be just watching you in return.

entries.subtitle: damnit, whole thing turns on where you stand
body: It seems like, standing here, above all, perspective is what truly matters...or how to look at it, at least..., luckily we can find some clues in projective geometry.

steps.text: Let's draw a line with three points on it.
Let's draw a second parallel line with three points on it.
Look closely, we can connect every point to its corresponding point and see that each of those connecting lines passes through the same point, which we can call the perspectivity point.

closing: So let's define perspectivity more formally.

Two sets of points $A_1, A_2, A_3$ and $B_1, B_2, B_3$ are perspective to one another with respect to a point $P$, when the sets can be put into one-to-one correspondence, so that any two corresponding points are joined by a line through $P$.
Point $P$ acts as the central viewpoint, which unites the two separate lines ($a$ and $b$) into a single correlated system.

entries.subtitle: peace of mind, favours rules
body: The formal definition and sketches already show us the obvious. To determine a line, we need two points, and that two lines will eventually meet somewhere, even if that meeting place is inconveniently located at infinity.
Now, conveniently, from six axioms, we can infer everything we want to know in the projective plane.

steps.text:
**Axiom 1**
Each pair of distinct points is joined by a unique line.

**Axiom 2**
Any two lines meet in at least one point. Parallel lines meet at infinity. (Contrary to the parallel postulate of Euclid)

**Axiom 3**
There exist at least four distinct points, no three of which are collinear. Points are collinear when they lie on the same line.

**Axiom 4 (Fano's axiom)**
The diagonal points of a complete quadrangle are never collinear.

**Axiom 5 (Desargues' theorem)**
If two triangles are perspective from a point, then they are perspective from a line.

**Axiom 6 (the fundamental theorem of projective geometry)**
If a projectivity leaves three distinct points on a line $l$ invariant, then it leaves every point on $l$ invariant.

title: numerical analysis and 50 lines of VEM in Julia

body: Recently stumbled upon a paper by Sutton, who implemented the virtual element method for the two-dimensional Poisson problem in exactly fifty lines of MATLAB.
This paper feels like the perfect opportunity to start frictionless, implement it myself, and go through each line, trying to understand the concepts.
